name: Rectangle
tagline: Move and resize windows in macOS using keyboard shortcuts or snap areas.
description:
Rectangle is a free, open-source window manager for macOS. It moves and resizes windows through keyboard shortcuts or snap areas, making repeatable layouts faster than manually dragging window edges into place.

Send a window to the left or right half of a screen, place it in a corner, center it, maximize it, or use a proportion that suits a particular display. This is useful when a browser, document, terminal, chat window, and reference material need consistent positions across a normal workday.

Rectangle changes window geometry rather than replacing the apps in those windows. Its value comes from learning a few layouts that match the work, while checking for conflicts with macOS shortcuts or another window manager before enabling overlapping controls.

## Features

- Move and resize windows with keyboard shortcuts or configurable snap areas.
- Place windows in common layouts including halves, corners, thirds, center, and maximize.
- Use a free, open-source utility that supports both Apple Silicon and Intel Macs running supported macOS versions.
- Configure window-management behavior around a personal set of repeated layouts.
- Upgrade separately to Rectangle Pro only if custom positions and its additional workflow features are needed.

## Where it fits

Rectangle fits people who repeatedly arrange two or more windows and want a lightweight keyboard-first way to do it. It is a natural companion for large displays, external monitors, or focused split-screen work.

It is unnecessary when macOS’s built-in tiling is sufficient. Keep its shortcuts small and memorable, especially when using other productivity tools that reserve the same key combinations.
